annotation.title_clean: Trustworthy AI in Aotearoa: AI Principles
annotation.title_en: Trustworthy AI in Aotearoa: AI Principles
annotation.authors_or_issuer: AI Forum New Zealand, Law, Society and Ethics Working Group
annotation.venue: AI Forum New Zealand (hosted on data.govt.nz)
annotation.summary_en: AI Forum New Zealand's March 2020 high-level voluntary principles for trustworthy AI in Aotearoa: fairness and justice, reliability/security/privacy, transparency, human oversight and accountability, and wellbeing. It stresses that existing laws still apply, references Te Tiriti o Waitangi, and says self-regulation does not replace government regulation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Five principles: fairness and justice; reliability, security and privacy; transparency; human oversight and accountability; wellbeing.
Existing NZ laws (privacy, consumer, liability, IP, human rights) continue to apply to AI.
Requires respect for Māori rights under Te Tiriti o Waitangi.
Technologies capable of harm should not be deployed until accountability and liability are determined.
Self-regulation is no substitute for democratically mandated law; calls on government to elaborate public-sector obligations.
